definitions.explanation: Warm air, especially as a meteorological term referring to a warm air mass or warm front.

definitions.gloss: warming up; idling to warm up (an engine)
definitions.explanation: The act of running an engine at idle to bring it to operating temperature before driving. Also written as 暖機.

examples.japanese: ⟦{南|みなみ}→南：00652_minami⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{暖気|だんき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{流|なが}れ{込|こ}んでいる→流れ込む：05748_nagarekomu⟧。
examples.english: Warm air is flowing in from the south.

notes:
{暖気|だんき} has two distinct uses: warm air (meteorology) and warming up an engine (automotive).

SENSE 1 — WARM AIR:
Used in weather reports and meteorology. Often paired with ⟦{寒気|かんき}→寒気：12433_kanki⟧ (cold air).
- {暖気|だんき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{流|なが}れ{込|こ}む→流れ込む：05748_nagarekomu⟧: warm air flows in
- {暖気|だんき}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{寒気|かんき}→寒気：12433_kanki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ぶつかる→ぶつかる：02412_butsukaru⟧: warm and cold air masses collide

SENSE 2 — ENGINE WARM-UP:
Running an engine at idle to bring it to operating temperature. Also written {暖機|だんき} (with the kanji for "machine").
- {暖気|だんき}⟦{運転|うんてん}→運転：01335_unten⟧: idling to warm up
- {暖気|だんき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{終|お}わる: the warm-up is finished

USAGE:
Modern cars generally do not require long warm-up periods, so this sense is becoming less common in everyday conversation.
